Build a lab from your own data

Source: R/toolkit-lab.R
new_lab.Rd

new_lab() writes an interactive lab (a learnr tutorial) that walks students through an IRT analysis of your dataset: the data, classical item statistics, dimensionality, model comparison, item fit, information, scoring and, when you give a grouping variable, DIF. Every number in the text, every answer check and every multiple-choice question is computed from the data when the lab is rendered, so the same lab works with any dataset and swap_lab_data() can replace the data later without touching the text.

Usage

new_lab(
  name,
  data,
  course = ".",
  items = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  data_title = NULL,
  story = NULL,
  sections = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

name

the lab's name: letters, digits, - and _.

data

the responses: a data frame or matrix, or the path of a file (.csv, .tsv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls, .sav, .dta, .sas7bdat or .rds). Items must be scored 0/1 or in ordered integer categories, unless you give a key. A frequency table (one row per response pattern with a freq or count column, such as mirt::LSAT7) is expanded to one row per person.

course

the course folder (see new_course()); the lab goes in its labs/ folder.

items

the item columns, by name or position. By default, every column whose values are whole numbers from 0 to 9 (other than group and ID-like columns), or the names of a named key.

group

optional grouping variable with two values, for the DIF section: a column name of data, or a vector with one value per row.

key

optional answer key for unscored multiple-choice responses, one value per item; the items are scored with mirt::key2binary().

title

the lab's title.

data_title

a short name for the data used in the lab's text, for example "the Grade 8 science test".

story

a paragraph that sets the scene, shown at the start of the lab.

sections

the sections to include, in order; see lab_section_types(). The default includes every section that suits the data ("dif" only with a group).

overwrite

replace an existing lab of the same name.

Value

The path of the lab folder, invisibly.

Details

The lab is a folder labs/<name>/ inside the course folder, holding <name>.Rmd and a data/ folder (responses.rds and lab.json). Edit the .Rmd freely; add_lab_section(), add_lab_exercise() and add_lab_question() add content, and check_material() runs every exercise's solution through its check.

See also

new_course(), swap_lab_data(), add_lab_section(), check_material(), preview_lab()

Examples

course <- file.path(tempdir(), "lab-demo")
new_course(course)
lab <- new_lab("lsat", data = expand.table(LSAT7), course = course,
               data_title = "the LSAT section 7 items",
               sections = c("intro", "classical", "models", "wrap-up"))
lab_outline(lab)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   id        type      title                     exercises questions
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr>                         <int>     <int>
#> 1 intro     intro     Meet the data                     1         0
#> 2 classical classical Classical item statistics         2         1
#> 3 models    models    Compare IRT models                2         1
#> 4 wrap-up   wrap-up   Where to next                     0         0
